title: Waterzooi
subtitle: Belgian creamy chicken and vegetable stew
excerpt: The great stew of Ghent: a whole chicken poached gently in a rich vegetable broth enriched with cream and egg yolks until the broth is velvety and the chicken is tender. Served in deep bowls with the vegetables and thick slices of bread.

recipe.sourceNotes: Waterzooi (from the Flemish words for water and to boil) is the defining dish of Ghent, one of Belgium's oldest and most celebrated cities. The original version, documented from the sixteenth century, was made with freshwater fish from the rivers running through Ghent; as overfishing depleted the rivers, chicken replaced the fish and became the standard. The version with chicken (poulet waterzooi) is now the most widely eaten; fish waterzooi (using freshwater or sea fish) survives as a specialty of coastal Flemish restaurants. The defining element is the enrichment of the broth with cream and egg yolks at the end, whisked in off the heat to create a liaison that thickens the broth without scrambling the eggs.

content.text: Poach the chicken at a gentle simmer, never a boil. Hard boiling makes the meat stringy. The cream and egg yolk liaison is added off the heat and the broth must not return to the boil once it is in or it will curdle. Whisk the cream into the egg yolks first, then add a ladle of hot broth to temper before adding to the pot.

items.preparation: jointed into 8 pieces; or use bone-in thighs and drumsticks
white and pale-green parts; cut into 3 cm rounds

content.text: Melt the butter in a large pot. Cook the onion, carrot, celery, and leek over medium heat for 8 minutes until softened but not coloured. Add the stock, bay leaves, and thyme. Add the chicken pieces and potatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered for 35 to 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.

Lift out the chicken pieces. Season the broth with salt and pepper. In a bowl, whisk the egg yolks and cream together. Add a ladleful of hot broth to the cream mixture and whisk to temper. Remove the pot from the heat.

Pour the cream and egg yolk mixture into the pot, stirring. Return the chicken pieces. Heat very gently without simmering for 2 minutes. Remove the bay leaves. Scatter with parsley. Serve in deep bowls with plenty of bread.
